H Cup Bra Size Guide — Fit, Sister Sizes & Best Bras

An H cup is a larger-than-average cup size that requires specific fit knowledge and the right bra styles to feel comfortable and supported. Whether you have just been measured as an H cup or have been wearing H cup sizes for years, this comprehensive guide will help you find bras that fit, flatter, and support your shape.

H cup wearers often struggle to find well-fitting bras in mainstream retail stores, where inventory skews toward smaller cup sizes. This guide covers how to measure for an H cup, sister sizes for fit flexibility, the best bra types for H cup breasts, and our top brand recommendations.

What is an H Cup?

An H cup is a bra cup size that is larger than the average. In US sizing, the cup progression typically goes A, B, C, D, DD/E, DDD/F, G, H. In UK sizing, the cup progression is A, B, C, D, DD, E, F, FF, G, GG, H. The exact letter depends on the sizing system being used.

An H cup generally corresponds to a bust measurement that is approximately 8 inches larger than the band measurement. For example:

  • 34H (US) = ~34 inch band, ~42 inch bust
  • 36H (US) = ~36 inch band, ~44 inch bust
  • 38H (US) = ~38 inch band, ~46 inch bust
  • 40H (US) = ~40 inch band, ~48 inch bust

H cups are not the largest available — cup sizes continue up to roughly a US P or UK K. But H is where many wearers start to find mainstream retail challenging and begin seeking specialty brands.

How to Measure for an H Cup

To determine your H cup size, you need two measurements:

1. Band Size (Underbust)

Wrap a soft measuring tape snugly around your ribcage, directly under your bust. Keep the tape level and parallel to the floor. Exhale normally and record the measurement in inches.

  • If the measurement is even, add 0 inches (or 4 inches if using the +4 method, though this is less accurate).
  • If the measurement is odd, add 1 inch (or 5 inches if using the +4 method).
  • Round to the nearest even number to get your band size.

2. Bust Size (Across the Nipple Line)

Wrap the measuring tape loosely around the fullest part of your bust — usually across the nipple line. Keep the tape level and do not compress the breast tissue. Record the measurement in inches.

3. Calculate the Difference

Subtract your band size from your bust size. The difference in inches corresponds to your cup size:

Difference (inches) US Cup Size UK Cup Size
1 A A
2 B B
3 C C
4 D D
5 DD DD
6 DDD / F E
7 G F
8 H FF
9 I G
10 J GG

For a more accurate measurement, use our Bra Size Calculator or visit a specialty bra fitter.

H Cup Sister Sizes

Sister sizes are equivalent cup volumes on different band sizes. If a particular band size feels too tight or too loose, you can adjust by going up or down a band while keeping the cup volume the same.

For a 36H (US), the sister sizes are:

  • 34I (US): One band smaller, one cup larger — same cup volume, tighter band.
  • 38G (US): One band larger, one cup smaller — same cup volume, looser band.
  • 34J (US) and 38DDD (US): Two bands and two cups in either direction, etc.

Sister sizing is useful when:

  • Your usual band is sold out.
  • You are between band sizes.
  • Your weight or body composition has changed slightly.
  • Different brands fit differently in the band.

Note: Sister sizes preserve cup volume but not necessarily fit. A bra with a snugger band may sit differently on your body, affecting how the cups position. Always try sister sizes with the same brand and style when possible.

Best Bra Types for H Cup Breasts

H cup wearers need bras engineered for support, lift, and shape. The following styles work best for larger cup sizes.

Full-Coverage Bras

Full-coverage bras have cups that fully encapsulate the breast, with no exposed cleavage at the top. This is the most supportive style for H cup wearers and is the foundation of any full-bust wardrobe. Look for reinforced cups, side support panels, and wide bands.

Side-Support Bras

Side-support bras have additional panels on the sides of the cups that push breast tissue forward, creating a more centered shape and preventing the dreaded "side spillage" that many H cup wearers experience. Elomi is the gold standard for side-support bras.

Minimizer Bras

Minimizer bras redistribute breast tissue to create a smoother, more streamlined silhouette under clothing. They can reduce the appearance of bust size by up to 2 inches. Look for minimizers specifically designed for fuller cups to maintain comfort.

Encapsulation Bras

Encapsulation bras have two distinct cups (as opposed to compression bras that press the breasts against the chest wall). Encapsulation is the gold standard for full-bust support because it allows each breast to be individually supported.

Bralettes (with caveats)

Modern bralettes designed for H+ cups — like those from Bratabase, Underdays, and Lively — can provide wire-free comfort and light support. Avoid flimsy bralettes designed for A–C cups, as they will not provide adequate support for an H cup.

Top 5 Brands for H Cup Bras

1. Elomi

Best for: H+ cup full-coverage and side-support bras

Elomi specializes in D+ cup bras, and their H cup styles are among the most popular in the world. The Cate, Molly, and Priya collections offer gorgeous prints, full coverage, and exceptional support up to a US 46J. Wide bands, side support panels, and reinforced straps make these a top pick for everyday wear.

Price: $55–$75 · Sizes: 32D–46J (US)

2. Bravissimo

Best for: H+ cup luxury bras and personal fittings

Bravissimo is a UK-based specialty retailer that focuses exclusively on D+ cup bras. They offer a wide range of styles — from everyday T-shirt bras to luxury lace — in cup sizes up to a UK L. Their personal fitting service is unmatched, and many wearers report finding their best-fitting bra ever at Bravissimo.

Price: $50–$120 · Sizes: 28D–40L (UK)

3. Goddess

Best for: H+ cup wireless and minimizer bras

Goddess specializes in wireless and minimizer bras for D+ cups, including H cup styles. The Kayla and Keira collections offer wire-free comfort and side smoothing, while the GD style is a popular minimizer. Sizes go up to a US 50J.

Price: $50–$65 · Sizes: 36C–50J (US)

4. Panache

Best for: H+ cup full-bust and sports bras

Panache makes some of the most popular full-bust bras on the market. The Envy and Clara collections are top sellers in H cup sizes, and the Panache Sport is widely considered the best high-impact sports bra for D+ cups. UK sizing runs to a K cup.

Price: $55–$80 · Sizes: 28D–40K (UK)

5. Bratabase

Best for: H+ cup wireless bralettes and everyday comfort

Bratabase is a relatively newer brand focused on wireless support for D+ cups. The Liberty Bralette is a wire-free style that supports up to a US 46H. Soft, structured, and surprisingly supportive for the size range.

Price: $48–$68 · Sizes: 30D–46H (US)

H Cup Bra Buying Tips

Follow these tips to find the best H cup bra for your body:

  • Get professionally fitted. Most women wear the wrong bra size, and H cup wearers are no exception. Visit a specialty bra boutique or use our Bra Size Calculator for an accurate measurement.
  • Try multiple brands. Sizing varies significantly between brands. A 36H in Elomi may fit differently than a 36H in Bravissimo.
  • Prioritize band fit. The band does 80% of the support work. If the band is too loose, the straps will dig in and the bra will not provide adequate support.
  • Look for wide, cushioned straps. Wide straps distribute weight across your shoulders and prevent the painful digging-in that many H cup wearers experience with thin straps.
  • Avoid plunges and balconettes for everyday wear. These styles can cause spillage for H cup wearers. Save them for special occasions and stick to full-coverage for daily support.
  • Replace regularly. H cup bras break down faster than smaller cup sizes due to the higher tension on the fabric. Plan to replace your most-worn bras every 6–9 months.

Common H Cup Bra Problems and Solutions

Problem: Straps Digging In

Solution: This is almost always a band issue, not a strap issue. If the band is too loose, the straps take on more weight. Try a smaller band size, or a bra with a wider, more cushioned strap.

Problem: Spillage at the Top or Sides

Solution: The cups are too small. Try a larger cup size or a sister size. Also, consider a side-support style that physically prevents side spillage.

Problem: Back Bulge

Solution: The band is too tight. Try a larger band size with a smaller cup (sister size). Look for bras with smoothing back panels designed for full busts.

Problem: Wire Digging Into Armpit

Solution: The cup is too small, pushing the wire into a pressure point. Try a larger cup or a different style with a wider wire channel.

Problem: Bra Riding Up in Back

Solution: The band is too loose. Try a smaller band, or a bra with a more structured back. The band should sit level and snug all day.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is an H cup bra size?

An H cup is a larger-than-average cup size that is roughly equivalent to a US FF cup (in some sizing systems) or a US 7th cup. It represents a bust measurement that is approximately 8 inches larger than the band measurement. H cups are less common than A–G cups, so finding bras in this size requires specialty brands like Elomi, Bravissimo, Goddess, and Bratabase.

How is an H cup measured?

To determine an H cup, first measure your band size (snug underbust) and bust size (across the fullest part of the breast). The difference in inches corresponds to your cup size. An H cup in US sizing equals approximately an 8-inch difference. In UK sizing, H is the 8th cup. Use our bra size calculator for a precise measurement.

What are the sister sizes of an H cup?

Sister sizes are equivalent cup volumes on different band sizes. For a 36H (US), the sister sizes are 34I (US) — go down a band, up a cup — and 38G (US) — go up a band, down a cup. Adjusting by one band and one cup preserves the same cup volume, though fit may vary slightly. In UK sizing, 36H has sister sizes 34HH and 38GG.

What kind of bra is best for H cup breasts?

H cup breasts need bras with full-coverage cups, wide bands, reinforced side panels, and strong straps. The best styles are full-coverage bras, side-support bras, encapsulation bras, and minimizers. Avoid balconette or demi cup styles which can cause spillage. Brands like Elomi, Bravissimo, Panache, and Goddess specialize in H+ cup support.

Are H cup bras hard to find?

Historically, H cup bras have been harder to find than smaller sizes, but the full-bust market has grown significantly. Today, brands like Elomi, Bravissimo, Goddess, Panache, Freya, and Bratabase all offer H cup styles both online and in select retail stores. Specialty boutiques and online retailers typically carry the widest selection.

Can I wear a regular bra in an H cup?

Yes — there is no functional difference between an H cup and any other cup size, only a volumetric one. You can wear any bra style that fits your H cup size and your breast shape. The key is to choose a bra designed for fuller busts (with appropriate support features) and to get a professional fitting or use our calculator to ensure proper size.
